warning: Indicators use different populations, years and definitions. They must not be combined into a causal fertility score without further validation.
headline_finding: German family aspirations remain materially higher than realised fertility, while housing, childcare and gendered care burdens show measurable security gaps. A nationally comparable baseline is still missing for several key dimensions.

indicators.label: Ideal number of children among young adults
indicators.interpretation: When respondents are asked to ignore obstacles, the average ideal family size is above two children.
indicators.limitation: Ideal family size is not the same as a concrete intention, forecast or entitlement to children.

source.title: Kinderwünsche, Care-Arbeit und Erwerbstätigkeit: Welche Rahmenbedingungen junge Erwachsene und Eltern brauchen

indicators.label: Intended number of children
indicators.interpretation: Intentions remained stable during the fertility decline, while near-term plans weakened among people aged 30–39.
indicators.limitation: Intentions include children already born and cannot be subtracted mechanically from annual total fertility rates.

indicators.label: Total fertility rate
indicators.interpretation: Period fertility is substantially below both replacement level and reported ideal family size.
indicators.limitation: The total fertility rate is a synthetic period measure and is affected by timing shifts; it is not the completed family size of a real cohort.

source.title: Zusammengefasste Geburtenziffer sinkt im Jahr 2025 auf 1,32 Kinder je Frau

indicators.label: Housing-cost overburden
indicators.interpretation: More than one in ten people lived in a household spending over 40% of disposable income on housing costs.
indicators.limitation: This indicator is not specific to prospective parents or families and does not prove an effect on fertility decisions.

indicators.label: 25-year-olds living with parents
indicators.interpretation: Delayed independent household formation may be relevant to partnership and family timing.
indicators.limitation: Living with parents can be voluntary and the statistic does not identify housing cost as the cause.

source.title: 30 % der 25-Jährigen wohnten 2025 noch im Haushalt der Eltern

indicators.label: Unmet childcare demand for ages 1 to under 3
indicators.population: families with children aged 1 to under 3
indicators.interpretation: Every fifth stated childcare need was not met in the national analysis; gaps were larger for low-income and non-German-speaking households.
indicators.limitation: The underlying data are older and must be refreshed before use as a 2026 baseline.

indicators.label: Childcare participation under age three
indicators.interpretation: The participation rate rose slightly while the number of children in care declined.
indicators.limitation: Participation is not the same as fulfilled demand, reliable opening hours or quality.

source.title: Zahl der unter Dreijährigen in Kindertagesbetreuung 2025 um 5,6 % gesunken

indicators.label: Employment rate of parents with a child under three
indicators.population: parents aged 15–64 with at least one child under three in household
indicators.interpretation: The realised employment gap is large and strongly gendered during early parenthood.
indicators.limitation: The measure includes voluntary choices and parental leave arrangements and does not by itself quantify an involuntary career penalty.

source.title: 39,7 % der Mütter mit einem Kind unter drei Jahren sind erwerbstätig

indicators.label: Planned parental-benefit duration
indicators.interpretation: Care-related leave remains highly unequal in duration.
indicators.limitation: Elterngeld receipt does not capture all unpaid care or identify the preferred division of each family.

source.title: Elterngeld 2025: Anteil der Eltern mit Elterngeld Plus auf Höchststand

indicators.label: Weekly housework time
indicators.population: working-age women and men in relationships
indicators.interpretation: Unequal routine housework can affect relationship satisfaction and the perceived cost of additional children.
indicators.limitation: Housework is only one component of total care and mental load.

source.title: Geteilt, gerecht, zufrieden? Aufteilung von Hausarbeit in Beziehungen

indicators.label: Comparable national family-formation health baseline
indicators.interpretation: A single comparable baseline linking fertility access, pregnancy care, birth experience, postpartum health and later family intentions was not identified in the initial official-source sweep.
indicators.limitation: This is a search finding, not proof that no relevant datasets exist.

indicators.label: Comparable non-take-up and administrative-burden baseline
indicators.interpretation: The initial sweep did not identify one current official national dataset covering entitlement, application friction, processing time and non-take-up across core family benefits.
indicators.limitation: Programme-specific evidence may exist and must be mapped separately.

priority_data_gaps: Current Germany-wide gap between ideal, intended, expected and ultimately realised family size by age, gender, parity, income and region
Current unmet childcare demand plus closure days, reduced opening hours and emergency backup availability
Prospective-parent housing affordability and time to obtain adequate housing
Motherhood and fatherhood earnings, pension and career effects by parity
Access, waiting times and outcomes for fertility, maternity and postpartum services
Administrative burden and non-take-up across family benefits
Relationship safety, support networks and time scarcity as family-formation constraints
